The circles $r=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ and $r=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $  intersect at points $O$ and $A,$ as shown above. What are the polar coordinates $(r,\theta )$ of the point $A?$ Express the polar angle $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ in radians.

$(r,\theta )=(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$)$
question.worked_solution:
First of all, we notice from the graph that the origin $O$ is an obvious first point of intersection. 

To find the second point of intersection, we set the equations of the curves equal to each other and solve for $\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } & =1 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the solution $\theta =\frac{\pi }{4}$ in the $1$st quadrant.

Now, we use the equation $r=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta $ to find the $r$-coordinate of the point $A:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, polar coordinates of the point $A$ are 

 

$$
(r,\theta )=(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},\frac{\pi }{4}).
$$
